reconstructed_theorem_text: For every real number m > 0, let Gₐ be the Borel Gaussian probability measure on ℝ with mean a and variance 1. Set μ = ½G₋ₘ + ½Gₘ and ν = ¼G₋ₘ + ¾Gₘ. Then m/2 ≤ W₂(μ, ν) ≤ m, where W₂(μ, ν) is the square root of the infimum of ∫ |x − y|² dπ(x, y) over all Borel probability measures π on ℝ² with first marginal μ and second marginal ν. The two real bounds are viewed as nonnegative extended real numbers.
objects: The real parameter m; the unit-variance Gaussian probability measures G₋ₘ and Gₘ; the two mixtures μ and ν; and their quadratic Wasserstein distance W₂(μ, ν).
domains: m lies in ℝ. The Gaussian measures and mixtures are Borel probability measures on ℝ. Couplings are Borel probability measures on ℝ². The inequalities are in the extended nonnegative reals.
quantifiers: For every m ∈ ℝ satisfying 0 < m, both inequalities hold. The distance uses an infimum over all couplings with the specified marginals.
assumptions: 0 < m; there are no other assumptions on m.
conclusion: The quadratic Wasserstein distance from μ to ν is at least m/2 and at most m, inclusively.
scopes: For each m, both mixtures are defined locally using the same two component Gaussians, and both bounds apply to the same pair (μ, ν). The coupling π is bound only within the distance definition.
constant_dependencies: The common variance 1 and the weights (1/2, 1/2) for μ and (1/4, 3/4) for ν are fixed; the means −m and m and the bounds m/2 and m depend only on m.
